exercises.name: Chin Tucks
exercises.summary: One of the key exercises for practising a more neutral head position.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person seen from the side, finger on chin, drawing the head straight back.
steps: Look straight ahead.
Imagine your head sliding backward along an invisible horizontal track.
Draw your chin backward to create a small double chin.
Keep your eyes level. Don't look down or tilt your head backward.
Hold for 3–5 seconds.
Relax for 2 seconds and repeat.
easier: Start without a wall if that feels easier. Don't force your head against it.
cautions: Keep the movement gentle. Do not tip your head down.
Stop if you feel dizziness, tingling or pain.
exercises.feel: A gentle effort in the front of your neck and possibly a stretch at the back.
exercises.instruction: Slide your head straight back to make a small double chin, hold, then relax.

exercises.name: Supine Chin Tucks
exercises.summary: A supported chin tuck lying down, so your neck muscles work without holding up your head.
exercises.instruction: Lying on your back, gently nod your chin in and press the back of your head into the floor.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating supine chin tucks.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Keep your head resting on the floor or a thin pillow.
Gently nod your chin in, as if making a small double chin.
Hold for about 5 seconds, then relax.
easier: Use a folded towel under your head for comfort.
cautions: Keep the movement small. Your head shouldn't lift off the floor.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Gentle Neck Rotations
exercises.summary: Slow turns to each side, stopping at the first comfortable stretch.
exercises.illustrationDescription: Four standing poses: facing forward, turning the head right, turning left, then back to centre.
exercises.startingPosition: Sit tall, shoulders relaxed, eyes looking forward.
steps: Slowly turn your head to the left, as though looking over your left shoulder.
Stop at the first comfortable stretch. Keep your chin level.
Hold for 3–5 seconds.
Return to the centre, then slowly turn right.
Repeat without moving your shoulders.
cautions: Don't twist until your chin reaches your shoulder if that feels uncomfortable.
exercises.instruction: Turn your head slowly to one side, return to centre, then turn to the other.

exercises.name: Side-of-Neck Stretch
exercises.summary: This targets the muscles along the sides of your neck.
exercises.illustrationDescription: Four standing poses: tilting the head toward one shoulder, back to centre, then toward the other shoulder.
steps: Sit tall and hold the right side of your chair with your right hand.
Keep your right shoulder down.
Slowly bring your left ear toward your left shoulder.
Keep your nose facing forward. Don't turn your head.
Hold for 15 seconds while breathing normally.
Return to the centre slowly.
exercises.switchSides: Hold the chair with your left hand and tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder.
cautions: Do not pull your head down. You should feel a gentle stretch, not pain.
exercises.instruction: Tilt your ear towards your shoulder until you feel a gentle stretch.

exercises.name: Back-of-Neck Stretch
exercises.summary: Gently stretches the muscles connecting your neck to your shoulder blade.
exercises.illustrationDescription: Four poses seen from behind: turning the head and opening the arms to stretch the back of the neck and shoulders.
steps: Sit tall and keep your right shoulder relaxed.
Turn your head approximately 30–45 degrees to the left.
Gently lower your chin toward your left armpit.
Stop when you feel a mild stretch along the back-right side of your neck.
Hold for 10–15 seconds, then return to the centre.
exercises.switchSides: Turn right and angle your chin toward your right armpit.
cautions: Keep your hands relaxed. Do not pull on the back of your head.
exercises.instruction: Lower your chin gently towards your chest and let the back of your neck lengthen.

exercises.name: Scapular Retractions
exercises.summary: Draw your shoulder blades together to support upright posture.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A view of a person's upper back, with arrows showing the shoulder blades moving toward each other.
steps: Sit tall with your arms resting by your sides.
Gently draw both shoulder blades backward and slightly toward each other.
Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Hold for 3–5 seconds.
Release completely and repeat.
easier: Squeeze more gently and hold for a shorter time.
cautions: Avoid arching your lower back, sticking your chest out excessively, or squeezing as hard as possible.
exercises.instruction: Draw your shoulder blades back and down, hold, then release.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Rows
exercises.summary: Strengthens the muscles between your shoulder blades that help you sit tall.
exercises.instruction: Pull the band towards your ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together, then return slowly.
exercises.repsGuide: Slow, steady pulls · about 2 seconds each way
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating resistance band rows.
steps: Anchor a light band at chest height, or loop it around your feet while seated.
Hold one end in each hand, arms straight in front.
Pull your elbows back alongside your ribs.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then return slowly.
easier: Use a lighter band, or stand closer to the anchor.
cautions: Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Check the band is secure before you pull.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Prone W Raises
exercises.summary: Works the muscles around the shoulder blades in a W position.
exercises.instruction: Lying face down, lift your arms in a W shape just off the floor, then lower.
exercises.repsGuide: Lift 2 seconds · hold 2 seconds · lower 2 seconds
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating prone w raises.
steps: Lie face down with a folded towel under your forehead.
Bend your elbows and pull them down and back so your arms make a W.
Thumbs pointing up, gently lift your arms a few centimetres off the floor.
Hold briefly, then lower with control.
easier: Lift one arm at a time.
cautions: Keep your neck long and your forehead on the towel.
Lift only as high as feels comfortable.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Prone Y Raises
exercises.summary: Works the muscles around the shoulder blades in a Y position.
exercises.instruction: Lying face down, lift your arms in a Y shape just off the floor, then lower.
exercises.repsGuide: Lift 2 seconds · hold 2 seconds · lower 2 seconds
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating prone y raises.
steps: Lie face down with a folded towel under your forehead.
Reach your arms forward and slightly out so your body makes a Y.
Thumbs pointing up, gently lift your arms a few centimetres off the floor.
Hold briefly, then lower with control.
easier: Lift one arm at a time.
cautions: Keep your neck long and your forehead on the towel.
Lift only as high as feels comfortable.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Prone T Raises
exercises.summary: Works the muscles around the shoulder blades in a T position.
exercises.instruction: Lying face down, lift your arms in a T shape just off the floor, then lower.
exercises.repsGuide: Lift 2 seconds · hold 2 seconds · lower 2 seconds
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating prone t raises.
steps: Lie face down with a folded towel under your forehead.
Stretch your arms straight out to the sides so your body makes a T.
Thumbs pointing up, gently lift your arms a few centimetres off the floor.
Hold briefly, then lower with control.
easier: Lift one arm at a time.
cautions: Keep your neck long and your forehead on the towel.
Lift only as high as feels comfortable.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Prone Cobra
exercises.summary: Strengthens the upper back and the muscles that draw the shoulders back.
exercises.instruction: Lying face down, lift your chest slightly and turn your thumbs out, then lower.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating prone cobra.
steps: Lie face down, arms by your sides, palms down.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lift your chest a few centimetres and turn your thumbs out.
Hold, then lower slowly.
cautions: Keep your gaze on the floor so your neck stays long.
Don't push up with your hands.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Wall Slides
exercises.summary: Trains your shoulder blades to move smoothly as you reach overhead.
exercises.instruction: Forearms on the wall, slide your arms up while keeping your shoulders down, then slide back.
exercises.repsGuide: Slow slides · about 3 seconds up, 3 seconds down
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating wall slides.
steps: Stand facing a wall with your forearms on it, elbows at shoulder height.
Slide your forearms up the wall.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Slide back down to the start.
cautions: Only go as high as you can without shrugging.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Wall Push-Up Plus
exercises.summary: A gentle push-up that ends with an extra push to strengthen the muscles around your shoulder blades.
exercises.instruction: Do a wall push-up, then push a little further so your shoulder blades spread apart.
exercises.repsGuide: Slow push-ups · add the extra push at the top
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating wall push-up plus.
steps: Stand an arm's length from a wall, hands on it at shoulder height.
Bend your elbows and bring your chest towards the wall.
Push back to straight arms.
At the top, push a little further so your upper back rounds slightly.
easier: Stand closer to the wall.
cautions: Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.summary: Builds steady control through your back and hips.
exercises.instruction: On hands and knees, reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back, then switch.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating bird dog.
steps: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back.
Keep your back flat and hips level.
Hold, return, and switch sides.
easier: Move only the arm, or only the leg.
cautions: Move slowly. Don't let your lower back sag.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.
exercises.switchSides: Halfway through, switch to the other arm and leg.

exercises.name: Wall Angels
exercises.summary: Slide your arms up and down to wake up the upper back.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person stands with arms raised in a goalpost shape, with arrows showing the arms sliding upward.
steps: Stand with your back against a wall, feet a small step forward.
Raise your arms into a goalpost shape, elbows bent.
Slowly slide your arms up as far as is comfortable.
Slide them back down. Keep your back gently against the wall.
easier: Do the movement standing away from the wall.
Only raise your arms partway.
cautions: Do not force your arms back against the wall.
Stop if you feel pinching or pain in the shoulders.
exercises.instruction: Back against the wall, slide your arms up and down like a slow snow angel.

exercises.name: Cat Cow
exercises.summary: Round and arch your spine slowly to ease stiffness.
exercises.illustrationDescription: Two poses on hands and knees: above, the back gently arched with the head lifted; below, the back rounded with the head lowered.
steps: Start on your hands and knees on a soft surface.
Breathe in as you gently let your belly lower and lift your gaze.
Breathe out as you round your back and lower your head.
Move slowly between the two positions.
easier: Try it seated: hands on your knees, gently arch and then round your back.
Make the movement smaller.
cautions: Skip the floor version if getting down or up is difficult.
Cushion your knees and stop if you feel pain.
exercises.instruction: On hands and knees, round your back up, then let it gently dip.

exercises.name: Seated Thoracic Extensions
exercises.summary: Gently mobilises the upper back without leaning over the backrest.
exercises.instruction: Sitting tall, cross your arms and gently lift your breastbone up and back, then return.
exercises.repsGuide: Slow movements · about 3 seconds each way
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating seated thoracic extensions.
steps: Sit towards the front of the chair, feet flat.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Lift your breastbone up and slightly back.
Return to sitting tall.
cautions: Keep the movement in your upper back, not your neck.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Thoracic Extension Over a Chair
exercises.summary: Lean back over your chair to open up the upper back.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person sits in a chair with hands behind the head, leaning back gently over the top of the backrest and looking slightly up.
steps: Sit back in a stable chair with a firm backrest.
Rest your hands lightly behind your head, elbows wide.
Gently lean back over the top of the backrest and look slightly up.
Return to sitting tall. Repeat slowly.
easier: Cross your arms over your chest instead.
Lean back only a little.
cautions: Use a chair that will not roll or tip.
Do not pull on your head or neck.
Stop if you feel pain.
exercises.instruction: Hands behind your head, lean back gently over the top of the backrest.

exercises.name: Shoulder Rolls
exercises.summary: Slow circles to ease tension across the shoulders.
exercises.illustrationDescription: Four standing poses showing the shoulders lifting toward the ears, then rolling back and down.
steps: Lift both shoulders gently toward your ears.
Roll them backward in a smooth circle.
Move your shoulders down and relax.
Repeat slowly. Don't move your head.
easier: Roll one shoulder at a time.
Make smaller circles.
cautions: Move slowly and breathe normally.
Stop if you feel pain.
exercises.startingPosition: Sit upright, feet flat on the floor, arms relaxed by your sides.
exercises.hold: No hold needed. Take about 3 seconds per circle.
exercises.instruction: Lift your shoulders, roll them back and down in slow circles.

exercises.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
exercises.summary: Helps address tightness across the chest that can accompany rounded shoulders.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person stands in a doorway with forearms on the frame, one foot forward, leaning gently through.
steps: Stand in an open doorway.
Place your forearms against the door frame, elbows around shoulder height or slightly lower.
Step one foot forward.
Gently move your chest forward until you feel a stretch across the front of your chest.
Keep your neck relaxed and avoid arching your back.
Hold for 15–20 seconds, then step back.
cautions: Stop if you feel pinching in the front of your shoulders or tingling down your arms.
exercises.instruction: Forearms on the frame, step through until you feel a stretch across the chest.

exercises.name: Standing Chest Opener
exercises.summary: Open the front of the chest after time spent hunched forward.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person stands tall with hands clasped behind the back, chest lifted, with an arrow showing the chest opening.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Clasp your hands behind your back.
Gently draw your shoulders back and lift your chest.
Hold and breathe slowly. Relax when the timer ends.
easier: Hold a towel between your hands instead of clasping them.
Place your hands on your lower back.
cautions: Keep your neck relaxed and avoid arching your lower back.
Stop if you feel pain.
exercises.instruction: Clasp your hands behind you and gently lift your chest.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Stretch
exercises.summary: Stretch the front of the hip, which can tighten with long sitting.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person stands in a long split stance with hands on hips, back leg straight, with an arrow at the front of the back hip.
steps: Stand tall and step one foot back into a split stance.
Place your hands on your hips.
Gently tuck your hips under and shift forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip.
Hold and breathe. Switch sides when prompted.
easier: Hold the back of a chair or your desk for balance.
Take a shorter step back.
cautions: Keep your front knee over your ankle.
Stop if you feel pain in your hip, knee or back.
exercises.instruction: Step one foot back, tuck your hips under and feel the front of the hip open.

exercises.name: Seated Figure Four
exercises.summary: Stretches the hips and buttocks after long periods of sitting.
exercises.instruction: Rest one ankle on the opposite knee and lean forward gently from your hips.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating seated figure four.
steps: Sit towards the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat on the floor.
Rest one ankle on the opposite knee.
Sit tall and lean forward slightly from your hips.
Hold, then switch sides.
cautions: Don't press down on your knee.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
exercises.summary: Stretches the back of the thigh.
exercises.instruction: Straighten one leg with your heel on the floor and lean forward gently.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating seated hamstring stretch.
steps: Sit towards the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat on the floor.
Straighten one leg, heel on the floor, toes up.
Keep your back straight and hinge forward slightly.
Hold, then switch legs.
cautions: Lean only until you feel a mild stretch.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Trunk Rotation
exercises.summary: Eases stiffness through the middle of your back.
exercises.instruction: Sitting tall, turn your upper body to one side, hold, then turn to the other.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating trunk rotation.
steps: Sit towards the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat on the floor.
Cross your arms over your chest or hold the chair back.
Turn your upper body to one side.
Hold, return to centre, then turn the other way.
cautions: Keep your hips facing forward.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.
exercises.switchSides: Halfway through, turn to the other side.

exercises.name: Chest Opener
exercises.summary: Opens the front of the shoulders after leaning towards a screen.
exercises.instruction: Clasp your hands behind your back and gently lift your chest.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating chest opener.
steps: Sit towards the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat on the floor.
Clasp your hands behind your back.
Draw your shoulders back and lift your chest.
Hold, then relax.
cautions: Keep your chin level.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: One-Arm Hug Stretch
exercises.summary: Stretches the back of the shoulder.
exercises.instruction: Bring one arm across your chest and hug it in with the other arm.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating one-arm hug stretch.
steps: Sit towards the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat on the floor.
Bring one arm across your chest.
Use the other arm to hug it gently closer.
Hold, then switch arms.
cautions: Keep your shoulder down, away from your ear.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
exercises.summary: Stretches the back of the upper arm and shoulder.
exercises.instruction: Reach one hand down your back and gently guide the elbow with the other hand.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating overhead triceps stretch.
steps: Sit towards the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat on the floor.
Raise one arm and bend the elbow so your hand reaches down your back.
Use the other hand to guide the elbow gently.
Hold, then switch arms.
cautions: Keep your head upright.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Forearm Stretch
exercises.summary: Relieves tension in the wrists and forearms from typing.
exercises.instruction: Arm straight, palm out, gently draw your fingers back with the other hand.
exercises.repsGuide: Hold 10 seconds · palm up and palm down · each side
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person demonstrating forearm stretch.
steps: Hold one arm straight in front, palm facing out.
Gently draw your fingers back with the other hand.
Hold, then turn your palm down and repeat.
Switch arms.
cautions: Keep the stretch gentle.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, numbness or tingling.

exercises.name: Sit-to-Stand
exercises.summary: Build everyday leg strength by standing up from a chair.
exercises.illustrationDescription: Two poses: a person sitting near the front of a chair leaning slightly forward, then standing tall in front of the chair.
steps: Sit near the front of a stable chair, feet hip-width apart.
Lean forward slightly and press through your feet to stand up.
Stand tall for a moment.
Sit back down slowly and with control.
easier: Use your hands on your thighs or the armrests to help.
Do fewer reps and rest between them.
cautions: Use a chair that will not roll. Avoid office chairs with wheels.
Stop if you feel dizzy or have pain.
exercises.instruction: Stand up from the chair without using your hands, then sit back down slowly.

exercises.name: Supported Calf Raises
exercises.summary: Rise onto your toes while holding a chair for support.
exercises.illustrationDescription: A person stands holding the back of a chair, rising onto the balls of the feet, with an arrow pointing up at the heels.
steps: Stand behind a stable chair and hold the backrest.
Slowly rise up onto the balls of your feet.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower your heels slowly back down.
easier: Rise only partway.
Hold the chair with both hands.
cautions: Keep a steady hold on your support.
Stop if you feel unsteady or have pain.
exercises.instruction: Holding the chair, rise onto your toes, then lower slowly.

routines.title: Desk Reset
routines.summary: A few desk stretches to break up sitting.

routines.title: Posture Refresh
routines.summary: Sit, then stand, to reset how you hold yourself.

routines.title: Stand-Up Break
routines.summary: Get out of your chair and open up hips, chest and shoulders.

routines.title: Steady Legs
routines.summary: Simple strength for standing, walking and climbing stairs.

routines.title: Full Movement Break
routines.summary: A longer session that moves everything, including some floor work.
